messages:
anya: Running into a weird issue where our python sample app keeps using an old org token after a customer rotates to a project-scoped key. It works for a few requests then starts getting 401s.
liam: is the app using the SDK or raw http calls?
anya: python SDK v0.9.2. The flow: login via CLI (stores org token), start app (no REDWOOD_API_KEY set so SDK picks up cached creds), rotate key in console to a project key, export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-project-777 and expect it to use that. Instead, after ~30s the app shows `401 insufficient_scope` and continues to call with the old org token.
reza: sounds like credential refresh + streaming interaction. Do you have streaming websocket connections or long-lived HTTP streams?
anya: yes, we maintain a server-sent-events stream to keep a model context warm. When token is rotated, the initial requests are fine, but the keep-alive renews using cached credentials.
liam: IIRC the Go SDK re-evaluates env vars on every new request but the python SDK caches a CredentialProvider which only reads env on init. Possible parity gap.
ops-bot: Note: customer on eu-west requested urgent workaround.
devtools-bot: Automated hint: consider adding `REDWOOD_FORCE_ENV_CRED=true` as a temporary override in sample apps.
anya: workaround I validated: explicitly pass the key to Client() constructor: `Client(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])` — that forces it. But that's poor ergonomics for quickstart.
reza: two things: 1) SDK change to prefer explicit env variable on every credential resolution, not just on init; 2) add a small in-memory watch that invalidates cached creds when env var changes or when CLI creds get rotated.  Also update docs to call out that long-lived streams may need a restart during rotation until SDKs are patched.
liam: agree. Also add an integration test that simulates rotation: start app, rotate token, set env, expect subsequent requests to use new token.
anya: can we also emit a lightweight runtime warning like: `Using cached org token; export REDWOOD_API_KEY to override or restart process` so customers know what's happening?
reza: yes, add that to SDK logs at info/warn level.
liam: I'm opening a RFC PR to standardize precedence and to introduce a new env: `REDWOOD_CRED_SCOPE_HINT=org|project` so CLIs and CI can explicitly declare which scope they expect. This avoids heuristic fallthroughs.
anya: nice. Also can we add `redwood creds show` to CLI for quick debugging (prints active token prefix, scope, cached path)?
devtools-bot: UX suggestion saved to backlog.
ops-bot: I'll relay the temporary workaround to support and the customer.
anya: thanks all — assigning followups: @liam SDK patch (parity + warning), @reza tests + doc update, I'll update sampleapp README with the explicit constructor example.
liam: will target patch for next minor release. :shipit:
